holidays.name: Cow Milked While Flying in an Airplane Day
holidays.description: A salute to the day a cow took to the skies and gave milk at altitude. Celebrate with a tall glass of milk, a dairy-themed snack, or a respectful moo toward the clouds.
holidays.origin: On February 18, 1930, a Guernsey cow named Elm Farm Ollie flew on a Ford Trimotor plane to the International Air Exposition in St. Louis. She became the first cow to fly in an airplane. Along the way, Elsworth Bunce milked her in flight, making her the first cow milked in the air.
holidays.funFact: The milk was reportedly sealed into paper cartons and parachuted down to spectators below, so some people got airdropped milk straight from the sky.

holidays.name: National Drink Wine Day
holidays.description: An unofficial holiday that invites you to pour a glass of your favorite wine, whether red, white, rosé or sparkling. Raise a toast with friends, or just enjoy a quiet glass on a winter evening.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has been celebrated each year on February 18 across the United States, and wine lovers have embraced it with tastings and toasts.
holidays.funFact: Winemaking is among the oldest human crafts. Archaeologists have found evidence of wine production in Georgia dating back roughly 8,000 years.
